method: Sep 3 live Power Stack overlay. Fresh creator/video ideas are treated as research triggers only; company filings, official releases and current market reporting determine promotion, scoring and theme rank.

newIdeas.name: Flex Ltd.
newIdeas.theme: Cloud + Power Infrastructure SpinCo · grid-to-chip AI infrastructure
newIdeas.thesis: Planned Q1 2027 Cloud and Power Infrastructure spin remains one of the cleanest power/thermal/data-centre pure-play setups; funded backlog and customer quality matter more than headline MW pipeline.

newIdeas.name: MP Materials
newIdeas.thesis: Real production and magnet economics remain preferable to pre-revenue sovereignty stories.

newIdeas.name: Lynas Rare Earths
newIdeas.theme: Non-China rare-earth processing + magnet supply chain
newIdeas.thesis: Highest-quality current non-China producer/processor in the queue; strategically relevant to Malaysia.

newIdeas.name: NCR Voyix
newIdeas.theme: Commerce-platform simplification + recurring software + cash-flow inflection
newIdeas.thesis: The investable case is recurring software/services and cash conversion, not congressional-trading headlines.

newIdeas.name: FirstCash Holdings
newIdeas.theme: Pawn demand + collateral credit + trade-down economy
newIdeas.status: Priority research / wait for better entry
newIdeas.thesis: Persistent U.S. same-store pawn growth is a clean lower-income stress signal, but the equity has already rerated.

newIdeas.name: Vertiv
newIdeas.thesis: UtilityInnovation Group adds microgrid controls, specialised switchgear and behind-the-meter power orchestration to Vertiv's grid-to-chip stack.

newIdeas.name: Cleveland-Cliffs
newIdeas.theme: US steel protection + domestic HRC + operating leverage
newIdeas.thesis: Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose to $286m and management expects about $575m in Q3 as domestic demand improves, imports remain subdued and higher steel pricing restores operating leverage. Strong tactical fit, but leverage/cyclicality keep it below higher-quality steel peers for core status.
newIdeas.catalysts: HRC pricing, tariff/import protection, Q3 EBITDA delivery, free-cash-flow generation and debt reduction.
newIdeas.risks: Steel-price reversal, auto/manufacturing slowdown, leverage and policy reversal.
newIdeas.researchNote: Best new tactical creator pick from the Sep 3 sweep; do not chase the Sep 2 surge.

newIdeas.name: Wells Fargo
newIdeas.theme: Higher-for-longer NII + loan growth + improving credit
newIdeas.thesis: Q2 net income reached $6.4b with $12.3b NII, double-digit loan/deposit growth, 15% ROE and improving charge-offs/CRE nonperformers. Higher yields help while credit remains controlled; they become a headwind if funding, delinquencies or loan demand crack.
newIdeas.catalysts: NII durability, curve steepness, loan growth, efficiency and benign credit.
newIdeas.risks: Consumer/CRE deterioration, deposit competition, recession and excessive long-rate pressure on borrowers.

newIdeas.name: Mastercard
newIdeas.thesis: Q2 net revenue grew 14%, purchase volume 10%, cross-border 12% and value-added services 20%. Exceptional compounder, but current valuation and consumer/travel exposure offer less immediate asymmetry than scarcity infrastructure or banks.

newIdeas.name: Palantir Technologies
newIdeas.thesis: Q2 revenue +93%, US commercial +149% and adjusted FCF margin 63% confirm extraordinary execution. The problem is price-duration sensitivity: high long/real yields can compress even elite growth multiples.
newIdeas.catalysts: AIP/US commercial growth, government contracts, FCF and durable yield relief.
newIdeas.risks: Multiple compression, decelerating growth and crowded positioning.

newIdeas.name: The Trade Desk
newIdeas.status: Turnaround watch / not promoted to priority
newIdeas.thesis: Q2 revenue grew just 3% while adjusted EBITDA and margin fell YoY. Platform-antitrust pressure on Amazon may improve the long-run competitive narrative, but execution must reaccelerate before the stock deserves a Power Stack upgrade.
newIdeas.catalysts: Revenue reacceleration, Kokai/platform execution, margins and open-internet share gains.
newIdeas.risks: Execution, ad-budget cyclicality, platform competition and high-rate software compression.

newThemes.name: AI Time-to-Power / Microgrids
newThemes.summary: Behind-the-meter generation, microgrid controls, specialised switchgear and power orchestration are becoming a distinct investable layer of the AI buildout.
newThemes.whyNow: Vertiv's UtilityInnovation Group acquisition converts time-to-power from an abstract grid bottleneck into a strategic M&A category.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Data centres can bridge slow utility interconnections with onsite generation and controls, allowing suppliers to monetise before full grid completion.
newThemes.nextTest: Customer-funded microgrid wins and competing vendor disclosures.
newThemes.watchlistAction: VRT research conviction stays 7.7; ETN/PWR/GEV remain differentiated higher-quality complements.

newThemes.name: AI Data-Centre Load Quality / Ghost Demand
newThemes.summary: The AI physical buildout is real, but headline requested megawatts are not equivalent to funded projects.
newThemes.whyNow: Large-load audits, deposits and funding screens increasingly separate real hyperscaler demand from speculative interconnection queues.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Suppliers with deposits, firm orders and completed sites deserve a premium over developers valued on future MW narratives.
newThemes.nextTest: Do verified loads fall while named-customer supplier backlogs remain firm?

newThemes.name: Consumer Stress / Trade-Down + Weak Hiring
newThemes.summary: Expensive fuel, high borrowing costs and softer hiring are squeezing financed discretionary demand before the economy has entered a clean recession.
newThemes.whyNow: ADP hiring softened while pawn/trade-down evidence remains persistent and refined-product prices stay extreme.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Autos, residential solar, travel and lower-income discretionary demand face the largest pressure; collateral-credit and value models gain relative resilience.
newThemes.nextTest: NFP plus Q3 consumer-credit and pawn data.
newThemes.watchlistAction: Raise the hurdle for TSLA/ENPH/F additions; FCFS remains an indicator/beneficiary, not a chase.

newThemes.name: US Steel Protection / Reindustrialization
newThemes.summary: Domestic steel is gaining a tactical earnings tailwind from strong HRC pricing, subdued imports and trade protection while infrastructure/manufacturing demand improves.
newThemes.whyNow: Cleveland-Cliffs reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $286m and expects roughly $575m in Q3, with management citing improving domestic demand, subdued imports and extending lead times.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Higher domestic steel pricing expands operating leverage for US producers but also raises input costs for downstream manufacturers.
newThemes.nextTest: Does Q3 EBITDA/FCF confirm the steel-price move rather than merely price it in?
newThemes.watchlistAction: CLF promoted to selective research; compare against NUE/STLD before any core allocation.

mainNews.title: Cleveland-Cliffs Q2 2026 results and Q3 EBITDA outlook
mainNews.implication: Operating leverage and debt reduction are becoming visible as domestic steel economics improve.

newThemes.name: Banks: Higher-for-Longer vs Credit Stress
newThemes.summary: Banks can benefit from higher rates and curve income only while deposit costs and borrower credit remain controlled. This is a quality/credit-selection trade, not a blanket bank beta trade.
newThemes.whyNow: Wells Fargo's Q2 showed $6.4b net income, $12.3b NII, double-digit loan/deposit growth and improving charge-offs/CRE nonperformers as long yields stayed elevated.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Moderately higher yields support NII and reinvestment; excessively high yields eventually weaken housing, CRE, consumer credit and loan demand.
newThemes.nextTest: Can credit remain benign if the 10Y approaches 5%?
newThemes.watchlistAction: WFC promoted to selective research, not a blind higher-rates trade.

mainNews.title: Wells Fargo reports Q2 2026 results
mainNews.implication: Strong NII and loan growth coexist with improving credit, supporting selective bank exposure for now.

newThemes.name: Always-On US Equities / Market Infrastructure
newThemes.summary: Near-continuous US equity trading is moving from proposal to operational implementation, creating a new market-infrastructure demand layer around exchanges, brokerage, market data, surveillance, clearing and overnight liquidity.
newThemes.whyNow: The SEC's Sept. 17 roundtable is explicitly focused on launch preparedness, overnight surveillance, settlement, resiliency, cyber and liquidity. Nasdaq's approved 23/5 schedule is planned to begin Dec. 6, 2026.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Longer trading hours can raise exchange/data/broker engagement but also require more resilient systems, surveillance and staffing; the beneficiaries depend on actual overnight volumes and economics.
newThemes.nextTest: Do overnight volumes and monetisation justify the added operating complexity?
newThemes.watchlistAction: Research NDAQ/IBKR/CBOE first for quality; do not treat 24-hour trading as automatically bullish for every retail broker.

mainNews.title: SEC announces agenda for 24-hour trading preparedness roundtable
mainNews.implication: The regulatory discussion has shifted toward operational readiness and implementation rather than whether extended trading should exist.

mainNews.title: Nasdaq says approved 23/5 trading is planned for December 6
mainNews.implication: A dated launch target creates a concrete catalyst for market-infrastructure research.

newThemes.name: Open Internet Adtech / Platform Antitrust
newThemes.summary: Regulatory pressure on dominant retail-media and ad-auction platforms could improve the strategic narrative for independent adtech, but it is not yet an earnings catalyst.
newThemes.whyNow: The Amazon advertising lawsuit creates a fresh competitive-policy angle just as The Trade Desk is attempting to repair weak execution.
newThemes.marketTransmission: If platform conduct is constrained, independent measurement/auction infrastructure may gain bargaining relevance; if TTD execution remains weak, the policy tailwind is irrelevant.
newThemes.nextTest: TTD Q3/Q4 reacceleration, not lawsuit headlines.
newThemes.watchlistAction: TTD stays turnaround research only until operating data improve.

refining-product-inflation.summary: The energy shock is increasingly a refined-product and transport-inflation problem rather than a simple crude-price trade.
refining-product-inflation.whyNow: US refineries are already running near 98%, crude/gasoline inventories fell and European gasoline/diesel cracks remain extreme.
refining-product-inflation.marketTransmission: Freight, airlines and consumers absorb the inflation tax while complex refiners/integrated producers retain pricing leverage; high product inflation also supports long yields.
refining-product-inflation.nextTest: Do cracks stay extreme while product supplied weakens?
refining-product-inflation.watchlistAction: Keep XOM/HIBISCS owned exposure; prefer refining bottlenecks over generic XLE FOMO.

long-end-duration-stress.summary: Long yields are becoming the central cross-asset variable as energy inflation, sovereign borrowing and private/corporate capital demand compete for the same duration capital.
long-end-duration-stress.whyNow: The US 10Y touched about 4.81% despite softer hiring while European and Japanese yields remain elevated. Weak growth is not producing the usual clean bond rally.
long-end-duration-stress.marketTransmission: Higher discount rates compress long-duration software/AI/SMR valuations, housing and financed consumption while rewarding cash-generative scarcity and selective banks.
long-end-duration-stress.nextTest: If oil falls but the 10Y stays near 5%, structural fiscal/capital-supply stress is becoming the dominant driver.
long-end-duration-stress.watchlistAction: Keep entry discipline high for duration-sensitive equities.

ai-financing-cash-conversion.summary: AI capex is now part of the rates story: the buildout consumes enormous debt/equity capital while suppliers with customer-funded orders and near-term cash conversion retain the best risk-adjusted economics.
ai-financing-cash-conversion.whyNow: High long yields and very large infrastructure financing needs make funding quality a first-order differentiator even as physical demand remains strong.
ai-financing-cash-conversion.marketTransmission: Debt-funded developers and distant cash flows face multiple/refinancing pressure; switchgear, grid, cooling and construction suppliers can monetise funded projects earlier.
ai-financing-cash-conversion.nextTest: Does issuance/funding cost continue rising while supplier backlogs stay strong?
ai-financing-cash-conversion.watchlistAction: Prefer customer-funded physical infrastructure over speculative AI duration.

fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.summary: Nitrogen scarcity and North American gas advantage remain strong, but farmer affordability and crowded equity pricing increasingly matter.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.whyNow: Global supply disruption supports nitrogen pricing while North American feedstock remains advantaged; CF's equity move already reflects much of the good news.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.marketTransmission: Low-cost nitrogen producers benefit first, then high input costs can reduce application rates and pressure farm economics.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.nextTest: Can margins remain high without causing severe farmer demand destruction?
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.watchlistAction: CF thesis strong; do not chase records.

energy-security-americas-lng.summary: Western Hemisphere crude, LNG and export infrastructure gain strategic value as Gulf supply routes remain unreliable.
energy-security-americas-lng.nextTest: Does contracting/export rerouting persist after conflict volatility cools?

software-relative-strength.summary: Software is separating into exceptional cash-generative AI winners and weaker leveraged/private-credit borrowers, but high yields still compress the whole duration complex.
software-relative-strength.nextTest: Can elite growth names hold estimates while weak software credit continues deteriorating?
software-relative-strength.watchlistAction: PLTR fundamentals are elite but valuation-sensitive; CRWD/CRM selective; TTD turnaround only.

gold-rates-antifiat.summary: Gold remains a structural fiscal/geopolitical hedge but real yields and USD still control the tactical entry.
gold-rates-antifiat.nextTest: Gold trend stabilization alongside falling real yields.

uranium-fuel-cycle.summary: Fuel-cycle scarcity remains structurally attractive but has less immediate cross-asset significance than rates, products and AI power this week.
uranium-fuel-cycle.watchlistAction: CCJ remains preferred quality uranium exposure.
